title: Cloud Foundations
content: Cloud computing delivers computing resources over the internet, on demand. KEY CONCEPTS: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS. Public/private/hybrid cloud. On-demand, pay-as-you-go, elasticity. WORKED EXAMPLE: Renting servers by the hour (IaaS) instead of buying hardware. PRACTICE: 1) Define IaaS/PaaS/SaaS. 2) Explain elasticity. 3) Compare public vs private cloud.
quiz_json: [{"q": "Which cloud service model provides virtualized computing resources like servers and storage over the internet?", "options": ["IaaS", "PaaS", "SaaS", "Hybrid Cloud"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) delivers virtualized computing resources such as servers and storage on demand."}, {"q": "What does elasticity in cloud computing refer to?", "options": ["The ability to pay only for what you use", "The ability to scale resources up or down automatically", "The use of private cloud infrastructure", "The delivery of software applications over the internet"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Elasticity means the cloud can automatically scale resources up or down based on demand."}, {"q": "Which statement best describes a public cloud?", "options": ["Cloud resources are shared and accessible over the internet", "Cloud resources are dedicated to a single organization", "A mix of public and private cloud environments", "Cloud services delivered only on-premises"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "A public cloud provides shared resources accessible over the internet to multiple users."}]

title: Core Cloud Services
content: The building blocks of cloud platforms. KEY CONCEPTS: Compute (VMs, containers, serverless), storage (object, block, file), databases (managed SQL/NoSQL), networking (VPC, load balancers). WORKED EXAMPLE: Serverless functions run code without managing servers, scaling automatically. PRACTICE: 1) Name 3 compute types. 2) Compare object vs block storage. 3) Explain serverless.
quiz_json: [{"q": "Which of the following is NOT a type of compute service in cloud platforms?", "options": ["Virtual Machines (VMs)", "Containers", "Serverless functions", "Block storage"], "correct": 3, "explanation": "Block storage is a type of storage service, not a compute service."}, {"q": "What is a key difference between object storage and block storage?", "options": ["Object storage is optimized for unstructured data; block storage is used for structured data.", "Object storage manages data as discrete units with metadata; block storage manages data in fixed-size blocks without metadata.", "Object storage is faster than block storage in all scenarios.", "Block storage cannot be used for databases."], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Object storage manages data as discrete objects with metadata, suitable for unstructured data, while block storage manages data in fixed-size blocks without metadata, suitable for structured data and low-latency access."}, {"q": "Which statement best describes serverless computing?", "options": ["It requires manual server management and scaling.", "It runs code without managing servers and automatically scales.", "It only supports SQL databases.", "It is a type of block storage service."], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Serverless computing allows running code without managing servers, with automatic scaling handled by the cloud provider."}]

title: Architecture & Scaling
content: Designing systems that scale in the cloud. KEY CONCEPTS: Horizontal vs vertical scaling, load balancing, auto-scaling, stateless design, CDN, caching, availability zones/regions. WORKED EXAMPLE: Auto-scaling adds servers during traffic spikes, removes them after — paying only for what's used. PRACTICE: 1) Compare horizontal vs vertical scaling. 2) Explain a CDN. 3) Describe stateless design.
quiz_json: [{"q": "What is the primary difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?", "options": ["Horizontal scaling adds more machines; vertical scaling adds more power to existing machines", "Horizontal scaling adds more power to existing machines; vertical scaling adds more machines", "Both add more machines but in different regions", "Both add more power to a single machine"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "Horizontal scaling involves adding more machines to handle load, while vertical scaling involves increasing the capacity (CPU, RAM) of an existing machine."}, {"q": "Which of the following best describes the purpose of a Content Delivery Network (CDN)?", "options": ["To balance load between servers", "To cache and deliver content closer to users to reduce latency", "To auto-scale servers during traffic spikes", "To store user session data"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "A CDN caches content at edge locations closer to users, reducing latency and improving performance."}, {"q": "Why is stateless design important for scalable cloud systems?", "options": ["It allows servers to store user sessions locally", "It enables easy addition or removal of servers without affecting user sessions", "It requires more powerful servers", "It eliminates the need for load balancers"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Stateless design means servers do not store user session information locally, allowing easy scaling by adding or removing servers without disrupting sessions."}]

title: Edge & Serverless
content: Modern cloud pushes compute to the edge. KEY CONCEPTS: Edge computing, serverless (functions, workers), cold starts, global distribution, latency reduction. WORKED EXAMPLE: Cloudflare Workers run code at edge locations near users, cutting latency (this platform runs on exactly this). PRACTICE: 1) Explain edge computing. 2) Define a cold start. 3) Describe serverless benefits.
quiz_json: [{"q": "What is the primary advantage of edge computing in modern cloud architectures?", "options": ["Centralizing data processing in one location", "Reducing latency by processing data closer to users", "Increasing cold start times", "Eliminating the need for servers entirely"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Edge computing reduces latency by running compute tasks closer to the user, improving performance."}, {"q": "What does a 'cold start' refer to in serverless computing?", "options": ["The initial delay when a serverless function is invoked after being idle", "A server crash due to overload", "The process of deploying code to the cloud", "The act of scaling serverless functions automatically"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "A cold start is the latency experienced when a serverless function is invoked for the first time or after being idle, as the environment initializes."}, {"q": "Which of the following is a key benefit of serverless computing?", "options": ["Users must manage server infrastructure", "Functions run only when triggered, reducing costs", "Compute is always running regardless of demand", "Requires manual scaling of resources"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Serverless computing runs functions only when triggered, which optimizes resource usage and reduces costs."}]

title: Cloud Data & Storage
content: Managing data in the cloud. KEY CONCEPTS: Object storage, managed databases, data replication, backups, KV stores, consistency models. WORKED EXAMPLE: A KV store gives fast global reads for config data; a SQL database handles transactions. PRACTICE: 1) Match storage type to use case. 2) Explain replication. 3) Compare KV vs relational.
quiz_json: [{"q": "Which cloud storage type is best suited for storing large unstructured data like images and videos?", "options": ["Relational databases", "Object storage", "Key-Value stores", "Managed SQL databases"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Object storage is optimized for storing large amounts of unstructured data such as images, videos, and backups."}, {"q": "What is the primary purpose of data replication in cloud storage?", "options": ["To increase data consistency by preventing updates", "To create multiple copies of data to improve availability and fault tolerance", "To compress data for faster transmission", "To convert relational data into key-value pairs"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Data replication involves creating multiple copies of data across different locations to ensure availability and fault tolerance in case of failures."}, {"q": "In which scenario would a Key-Value (KV) store be preferred over a relational database?", "options": ["Handling complex transactions with multiple table joins", "Storing configuration data requiring fast global reads", "Running SQL queries with strong consistency", "Managing relational data with strict schema"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "KV stores provide fast, scalable access to simple key-value pairs, making them ideal for configuration data with global read requirements, unlike relational databases which handle complex transactions."}]

title: Security & Cost
content: Running cloud safely and economically. KEY CONCEPTS: IAM (identity/access), encryption, secrets management, cost optimization, reserved vs on-demand pricing, monitoring/observability. WORKED EXAMPLE: Storing secrets in a managed vault (not code) prevents credential leaks. PRACTICE: 1) Explain IAM. 2) Name a cost-optimization tactic. 3) Describe secrets management.
quiz_json: [{"q": "What is the primary purpose of IAM (Identity and Access Management) in cloud security?", "options": ["To encrypt data at rest", "To control who can access cloud resources", "To monitor cloud costs", "To store secrets securely"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "IAM manages user identities and access permissions to ensure only authorized users can access cloud resources."}, {"q": "Which of the following is a common cost-optimization tactic in cloud computing?", "options": ["Using on-demand pricing exclusively", "Storing secrets in code", "Purchasing reserved instances", "Disabling monitoring and observability"], "correct": 2, "explanation": "Purchasing reserved instances allows you to save money by committing to use cloud resources over a longer term, reducing costs compared to on-demand pricing."}, {"q": "Why is storing secrets in a managed vault preferred over embedding them in code?", "options": ["It improves application performance", "It prevents credential leaks", "It reduces encryption overhead", "It increases on-demand pricing"], "correct": 1, "explanation": "Managed vaults securely store secrets separately from code, reducing the risk of credential leaks and improving security."}]

title: Grandmaster — Cloud Architecture
content: Designing robust, scalable cloud systems. KEY CONCEPTS: Microservices, containers/Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, multi-region, disaster recovery, the well-architected framework. WORKED EXAMPLE: Infrastructure as code lets you rebuild an entire environment from a script. PRACTICE: 1) Explain infrastructure as code. 2) Define disaster recovery. 3) Describe multi-region design.
quiz_json: [{"q": "What is the primary benefit of using infrastructure as code in cloud architecture?", "options": ["It allows rebuilding an entire environment from a script", "It eliminates the need for disaster recovery plans", "It ensures all services run in a single region", "It replaces microservices with monolithic applications"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "Infrastructure as code enables automated, consistent, and repeatable environment setup by defining infrastructure through code scripts."}, {"q": "Which of the following best describes disaster recovery in cloud systems?", "options": ["A strategy to recover from failures and minimize downtime", "A method to deploy containers using Kubernetes", "A framework for designing microservices", "A technique to scale applications within a single region"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "Disaster recovery involves strategies and processes to restore systems and data after failures or disasters, ensuring business continuity."}, {"q": "Why is multi-region design important in cloud architecture?", "options": ["It improves availability and disaster recovery by distributing resources across multiple geographic locations", "It simplifies infrastructure by using a single data center", "It eliminates the need for containers and microservices", "It reduces the use of infrastructure as code"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "Multi-region design enhances system resilience and availability by distributing workloads and data across different geographic regions, reducing the impact of localized failures."}]

title: King Level — Cloud Strategy
content: At King level you drive cloud strategy and transformation. KEY CONCEPTS: Cloud migration strategy, vendor selection, cost governance, cloud-native transformation, balancing lock-in vs capability. WORKED EXAMPLE: A company re-architects cloud-native to cut costs 60% and ship 5x faster. PRACTICE: 1) Design a migration plan. 2) Address vendor lock-in. 3) Build a cloud cost-governance model.
quiz_json: [{"q": "What is a primary goal of cloud-native transformation at the King level?", "options": ["To reduce costs and increase deployment speed", "To maintain legacy systems without change", "To avoid any vendor lock-in at all costs", "To prioritize on-premises infrastructure"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "Cloud-native transformation aims to reduce costs and increase deployment speed, as demonstrated by the example of cutting costs by 60% and shipping 5x faster."}, {"q": "When balancing vendor lock-in versus capability in cloud strategy, what is a key consideration?", "options": ["Choosing the vendor with the lowest initial cost regardless of features", "Avoiding all vendor lock-in even if it limits capabilities", "Finding a balance between leveraging vendor capabilities and managing lock-in risks", "Ignoring vendor capabilities to focus solely on open-source solutions"], "correct": 2, "explanation": "A key part of cloud strategy is balancing the benefits of vendor capabilities with the risks of lock-in, rather than completely avoiding lock-in or ignoring capabilities."}, {"q": "Which component is essential in building a cloud cost-governance model?", "options": ["Tracking and managing cloud resource usage and expenses", "Eliminating all cloud spending to reduce costs", "Focusing only on initial migration costs", "Ignoring cost metrics in favor of speed"], "correct": 0, "explanation": "Effective cloud cost-governance involves tracking and managing cloud resource usage and expenses to control costs over time."}]
